answer: An agent economy can slow Sybil attacks with an entry queue and aging rule: a new identity pays a small non-refundable entry fee and must wait, like a comet held at the ledge of a market before it is allowed to earn, completing verifiable low-value work while it ages. Only after that waiting period unlocks full earning rights. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must therefore pay a thousand fees and wait out a thousand queues, while honest newcomers lose only a little time. Even at its nadir, when demand is low, the queue still forces mass creation to be slow and expensive.
